summary: Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Arizona State University (B.A., ~1961–1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D., ~1966–1972). He served as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University from ~1972 to 2010.

Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hamburg and completed his PhD at the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

Jim Taylor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University in 1989 and served as a Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and has been a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim works in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams and others. She held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University.

Jinbo Shi specializes in linguistics, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang. He has held positions at CASS, Minzu University, North Minzu University, and Ningxia University.
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts as professor (教授) at both National Central University and Fo Guang University, attested in 2010.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He held positions at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2006), where he also served as Director (attested 2009–2010).

Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist educated at National Taiwan University and Indiana University (Ph.D. ~1965–1969). He was a Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and Correspondence Research Fellow at Academia Sinica.
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) was a linguist and historian who studied at Tsinghua University from ~1928 to 1932. He later held an academic post at Minzu University of China.

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University and Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held appointments at the University of Virginia and as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia.

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado under Paul W. Kroll. She held posts at Colorado, City University of Hong Kong, and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Jinshi Fan works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Su Bai (~1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and has held a post at Lanzhou University as professor and doctoral supervisor.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He served as deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and as a Researcher (Professor) at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe (1883–1959) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1904 to 1907. He held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita (1920–2009) was a Tibetologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1940–1943). He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1993).

Jiro Murata (1895–1985) was a scholar of archaeology and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920). He held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College, from ~1962 to 1967.

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. A University of Tokyo graduate (~1949–1953), he worked at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1988) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2008).
